The energy (1/2)(rho|v|^2 + |grad phi|^2/alpha) then changes by (theta-1/2)(rho|dv|^2 + |d grad phi|^2/alpha). The statements instead write (theta-1/2) times half of that quantity. issues.title: Numerical-dissipation coefficient in the energy identities is off by a factor of 2

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume rho^n >= 0 a.e. and state coercivity on H^1_0(D), or on H^1(D)/R, via Poincare's inequality.

issues.title: Coercivity on H^1 is false without boundary conditions and nonnegative density
issues.why_classification: Standard local hypotheses (boundary conditions, positivity) fix it with no change to method or scope.

issues.failure_explanation: If delta E^{n+1} > E_kin^{n+1}, the quantity under the square root is negative, so the momentum rescaling is undefined. Even when capped, reducing kinetic energy cannot absorb the excess, so the promised discrete energy balance after restart is not delivered. The bound in cor:added-3 scales with alpha, which is 10^12 in the experiments, so the excess is not shown to be small.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Clip the factor at zero (or limit the restart) and state that energy balance is restored only when delta E <= E_kin, or adjust the internal or potential energy instead.
issues.overall_effect: The restart-with-relaxation procedure is ill-defined in a nonempty regime and its energy guarantee fails there.
issues.title: Relaxation step is undefined when the potential-energy increase exceeds the kinetic energy
issues.why_classification: Well-definedness can be restored, but the energy-restoration guarantee must be weakened or replaced by a different mechanism.
